## STEP 1 — Strategy Analysis

Assembled from the recorded specification (`app/strategy_research/specs.py`); the engine
implementation is the frozen, auditable source of truth.

- **Indicators:** Hull MA(55): WMA(2*WMA(close,27) - WMA(close,55), 7)
- **Entry (long):** HMA rising (HMA_t > HMA_{t-1})
- **Entry (short):** HMA falling (HMA_t < HMA_{t-1})
- **Exit:** implicit - stop-and-reverse; flips on the opposite HMA slope; flat only during warm-up
- **Filters:** none (primary deadband = 0)
- **Parameters (canonical defaults):** length=55
- **Risk management:** none (no stop/target); fixed full-notional; risk % NOT optimised
- **Position sizing:** single-asset, fixed full-notional long/short
- **Implicit assumptions (the real targets of testing):**
- a reduced-lag MA (Hull) would track trend turns faster and rescue the fragile MA-trend family
- REFUTED: at fixed n=55 the Hull construction is WEAKER than SMA/EMA/WMA slope; shorter lag increased whipsaw/turnover and drawdown
- FROZEN formula: half=floor(n/2), sqrt_p=round(sqrt(n))
- SENSITIVITY ONLY (excluded from the primary): n in {20,34,89,100}, deadband in {0.05%,0.10%}
- SINGLE-ASSET SCOPE; daily bars; volume not used
- **Script-integrity / look-ahead check:** HMA uses only trailing closed bars; slope read on completed candles; engine shifts positions forward one bar - no repaint, no look-ahead.

## STEP 2 — Falsifiable Hypothesis

**H-028.** *This rule produces positive risk-adjusted returns net of realistic costs,
and this edge (a) survives walk-forward out-of-sample, (b) generalizes across assets not used to
select its parameters, and (c) is not explained by the number of parameterizations tried
(data-snooping budget = 1 configuration(s)).*

**Kill criteria (pre-committed, frozen before any run):** **Not Supported** if the out-of-sample
**deflated Sharpe < 0.95**, **or** the edge appears in a minority of asset/cost
conditions, **or** it fails to beat **buy-and-hold** and **matched random-timing (95th percentile)**
on risk-adjusted terms. **Graveyard** if out-of-sample max drawdown exceeds the
60% gate or fewer than 30 trades occur.

## Contribution to M-001 (documented rejection — NOT an active strategy)

This hypothesis was pre-registered and **rejected**. It is kept as evidence, not as a tradeable
strategy: it is **not enabled for paper trading and not connected to any broker or live execution**.

**Finding (links to M-001).** The pre-registered question was whether a *reduced-lag* moving
average (Hull) rescues the fragile MA-trend family (M-001). It does not:

- **Reduced MA lag did not rescue the trend family** — verdict **Graveyard** (OOS max drawdown 63.7%,
  > 60% gate; beats neither buy-and-hold nor matched random-timing; deflated Sharpe 0.657 < 0.95).
- **Shorter lag increased whipsaw and cost** — across the sensitivity periods, turnover rose
  monotonically as lag fell (n=100 → 220 trades … n=20 → 900 trades) and risk-adjusted performance
  fell with it; deadband filters did not fix it.
- **The Hull construction was weaker than SMA, EMA and WMA** at the same fixed n=55 (HMA OOS Sharpe
  +0.0103 / DSR 0.657, the worst of the four; SMA +0.0254, WMA +0.0240, EMA +0.0155) — even at
  near-identical turnover to SMA, so the Hull overshoot produced lower-quality entries and deeper
  drawdowns, not merely more of them.

This **sharpens M-001**: MA-trend fragility is intrinsic to the family, and lower lag makes it worse,
not better — a reusable prior for the next "faster/smoother MA" product.

**Full evidence:** [`studies/H-028_hull_ma_slope_trend_STRESS_TEST.md`](./studies/H-028_hull_ma_slope_trend_STRESS_TEST.md)
(walk-forward OOS, per-market, regime, sensitivity, ablations/comparators, deflated Sharpe, BH-FDR over the 10-variant family — none survive).
